chapter: Clarinet and lessons with Jim Humphrey
title: Humphrey's method book and lost music; no photographs
summary: Russell asks about the lesson book and Humphrey's compositions, which Robinson threw away; he has no photos of his bands.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Did you have any book when you took lessons from Professor Umphrey? I had a big book, yeah. I don't know what become of it, yeah. You don't remember the name of it?
Yeah, let me see, I don't know if I got the name.

Method book, yeah, exactly, yeah. I had some of his pieces. And he wrote them? Yeah, yeah. That he wrote out? And I just tore them up, you know. I said, sure, I don't think that'll be any good for me anymore.
Yeah, I wish we could find some of them. Yeah, yeah, that's all right. We'd like to have them. Put them in our library up at Tulane now, if we could find something like that.

I had some good done, a marching thing, you know. Like all the soldier boys and all such is that, you know. Yeah. And music. Let me see. I don't think I saved any of them things. And pieces. Yeah, I had a gang of them. I had even a book. I don't know what I did with them. They're not even here. I don't think I put them up anywhere, you know where I could get them. If you'd ever find something like that, we'd be glad to buy it from you too and tell you to. I'd be glad for you to have it. Searching around, I might look and find something.
You might find something like that. I'll stop someday in a few months.
Maybe you'll come across it sometime. I'd like for you to stop.

Things are still clustered up, you know. Yeah, I know how it is. My place is the same thing. Yeah, look at things. I've got things stuck up everywhere. Yeah, that's right. Do you have any photographs of your old bands? No. The band, your own band that you played up in the country or down here? No, I haven't got none of them.
